Laya results

Source: R/results.R
laya_result.Rd

A laya_result is a list with model, answers (one entry per question, in question order) and usage (token accounting and truncation flags), in the Python SDK's shape. Each answer has type, confidence, answer_confidence and action$act_probability, plus:

Usage

# S3 method for class 'laya_result'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

laya_probabilities(x)

laya_answer(x, id)

# S3 method for class 'laya_batch_result'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A laya_result or laya_batch_result.

row.names, optional

Ignored; part of the as.data.frame() generic.

...

Unused.

id

A question id.

Value

as.data.frame() returns a data frame with columns id, type, answer (the label, the score or TRUE/FALSE, as text), value (the chosen label's probability, the score, or P(true)), confidence, answer_confidence, act_probability and abstention. laya_probabilities() returns columns id, type, option and probability (for noul questions, options "false" and "true").

Details

  • choice: choice (the top label) and probabilities (per label);

  • score: score (the expected level, from 0 to levels - 1), legend and probabilities (per level, keyed "0", "1", ...);

  • noul: noul (the probability the statement holds).

With min_confidence, answers also carry abstention and abstention_threshold; from laya_predict_long(), window.

as.data.frame() gives one row per question; laya_probabilities() one row per option; laya_answer() extracts one answer. A laya_batch_result (from laya_predict_batch()) is a list of laya_results whose data-frame forms carry a state_id column.

Examples

if (laya_model_available()) {
  res <- laya_predict("Refund me now!", laya_preset("triage"))
  as.data.frame(res)
  laya_probabilities(res)
  laya_answer(res, "intent")$choice
}
